doc.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025

title: Four-track recording and the mono Four Seasons sound
summary: He describes four-track half-inch tape, sound on sound overdubbing for The Four Seasons, and why early records sound best in mono.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: At that time what was the technology in a good studio? How many tracks were you –
And you had two inch – one inch tape? © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

No it was half inch tape. Four track was half inch. And basically we would cut the tracks and sometimes we’d use two tracks. We’d put the rhythm on one track, the horns on another track. Sometimes we would record on all four tracks then mix it down and sort of overdub on top of it. But we were sort of in the embryonic stages of piecing records together as opposed to doing them live.

I have a rather silly anecdote. Years go I was in a dentist’s office. And they had a radio station on and I kept thinking something’s off here. And you know it was low, I couldn’t – and then a Four Seasons record came on. And I’m going, all I’m hearing is the singing. And what it was is one of their speakers was out. So I’m like oh my God, they were like panned hard left and hard right. That was on purpose I guess.

Well the way we would record The Four Seasons, we’d record a track and then we’d overdub on the track, and then after we did all the overdubs on track we’d mix it down to a mono and put the mono – we’d copy it onto the four track. Then we would do the background voices. The background voices were done without the lead. So we would do the background voices, then we would do sound on sound. As we were recording the double track we would be doing it in conjunction with playing, so now we have two tracks. Frankie would then sing the lead and if he had to double he still had the track to double, again sound on sound, and we’d have one track to do strings and horns. So back then the four tracks only made mono records. So when stereo came out to try to re-create it, the only thing that they did was they split it up sort of crazy. But the early Four Seasons records sound best as monos.

Did you at the time, that you and the engineers – I think I know the answer to this, but did you ever speculate like, “Oh, if we only had” and fill in the blank, like that piece of gear that’s sitting behind you. If we only had more tracks. If we only could do this.

Well it’s funny about inventions. You know you didn’t know you needed a can opener until somebody put one together. You know you’d go and you’d figure out maybe I’ll get a screwdriver or whatever it was. I’m using this as a sort of ridiculous kind of illustration. But the fact is you don’t know you need something until somebody shows up with it and says, “Oh boy this is handy.”
